correctness.rationale: The dispersion relation is stated with the exact two-layer finite-depth hypotheses. Euler's partial-fraction identity gives \(D(y)=D_0+2y\sum_{j,n}\rho_j h_j/(h_j^2y+\pi^2n^2)\), so \(D'(y)>0\) and \(D''(y)<0\). With \(H=D-yD'\), \(H>0\) and \(H'=-yD''>0\), \(R=AD'/H\) is strictly decreasing from \(T_c\) to zero. The exact derivative identity \(F'=H(T-R)/D^2\) proves either strict increase for \(T\ge T_c\) or exactly one positive minimum for \(0<T<T_c\). The large-wavenumber asymptotic \(F\sim Tk/(\rho_l+\rho_u)\) ensures the stationary point is global.

value.rationale: The minimum phase speed is the critical speed for resonance with a translating forcing and is used to organize capillary-gravity wave behavior. Proving exactly one positive minimizer excludes competing critical wavelengths across all admissible finite depths and densities, while the complementary monotonicity theorem gives a complete parameter classification. This is a structural global result beyond the already-known endpoint threshold and is not merely a numerical curve fit.
